subject: GCP private offer — commit burn plan & ops onramp
messages:
From: Priya Shah <procurement@orbitalai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <gcp-partner-sales@google.com>, finance@orbitalai.com
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer — kickoff and drawdown cadence

Hi Markus / Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. OrbitalAI is ready to accept the private offer but procurement needs an explicit monthly "commit burn" plan for our internal finance team and cloud chargebacks. Can you confirm: 

- Which SKUs will be consumed against the private offer (we need the mapping for our FinOps tags)
- The monthly drawdown cadence you recommend (calendar month vs 30-day window)
- Invoice timing and whether GCP Marketplace will show drawdown usage or Redwood will invoice us directly

We attached a stub of the consumption profile we expect for Q4 — start low, ramp after model tuning. Please send a proposed drawdown table and any required PO wording.

Attachments: rdw_commit_schedule_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Sr. Procurement Manager | OrbitalAI
procurement@orbitalai.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <procurement@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — kickoff and drawdown cadence

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers up front, and an attached draft table that maps your expected consumption to the private-offer SKUs. Highlights: 

- SKU mapping: compute and inference token SKUs are listed in tab "SKU_map". We'll bind those to the PO.
- Drawdown cadence: we recommend calendar-month drawdown with a 3% buffer for shortfalls; if you prefer exact 30-day rolling windows we can do that but it complicates GCP billing reconciliation.
- Invoicing: Redwood will submit monthly reconciliation statements to you; marketplace will reflect consumption but your invoice/payment is handled via the private-offer mechanism (signed PO + RDW invoice).

See attached: rdw_commit_schedule_v1.xlsx (updated) and the PO wording we typically ask for.

Questions for our side: Marissa / Jonas, can you ensure finance is okay with a monthly reconciliation statement and a one-month net-30 payment term? Ben — can you confirm if we need to include the GCP offer ID on the PO?

Thanks — sending updated attachments.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <procurement@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — kickoff and drawdown cadence

Thanks Priya — and thanks Markus for the draft. From finance ops perspective: 

- Monthly reconciliation + net-30 is fine. We'll produce a monthly usage statement and a single invoice for the committed amount; any overage/underdraw will be reconciled next month per the table.
- Please include the GCP offer ID on the PO; that speeds marketplace mapping.
- On buffers: propose we include an optional 3% top-up line item that OrbitalAI can draw pre-approval.

Action items:
- OrbitalAI: confirm preferred cadence (calendar month ok?) and sign the PO (we'll attach a PDF to the next email).
- Redwood: finalize the drawdown worksheet and include the exact SKU IDs.

Laura (CS) — please add a short ops playbook for the onboarding week that shows who to contact if drawdown doesn't appear in Marketplace.

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick operational note to close the loop. Per the signed PO and our private-offer process: 

- Drawdown visibility: GCP will display marketplace consumption lines that reference the private offer ID, but Redwood will also push a monthly reconciliation CSV to OrbitalAI that lists SKU, units, tokens, and the amount drawn against the committed balance. That CSV is what your FinOps team should import.
- Billing of the 3% buffer: the buffer is not invoiced up front. It's reserved as an optional allowance; you'll only be billed if consumption exceeds the committed amount in a month.
- Next steps: Redwood will provision the billing mapping and share the reconciliation sample (CSV + mapping guide) by EOD Thursday. Amit (Google) — please confirm any Marketplace timing constraints we should be aware of.

Attaching the final rdw_commit_schedule_v1.xlsx (with SKU IDs) and a short reconciliation example.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Revenue Platforms | Redwood Inference
